notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-442dc5 (issue #1391). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance, with one caveat that is not the extraction's fault. Two of the three recorded artifact hashes match byte for byte: the arXiv v4 PDF d37e986e...c0bd5c and the v4 e-print ff665124...60bdb4 (a nine-file LaTeX project with macros.sty). The third, for the published Cambridge PDF, cannot be reproduced by anyone: Cambridge Core watermarks each download with the requesting IP address and a timestamp ('Downloaded from ... IP address: ..., on 23 Sep 2026 at ...'), so two downloads in the same minute differ from each other and from the recorded 62d523a5...39e13. The file is the right article and its page tree reports the 79 pages the extraction read; the hash simply is not a check anyone can repeat, and the record should say so.

Numbering and coverage. macros.sty declares \numberwithin{thm}{subsection} and hangs every statement environment on the thm counter, so numbers are section.subsection.n. Simulating that across the seven included files gives 111 numbered statements, with the appendix lettered A, B, C (2, 7 and 6 statements), and it reproduces the kind as well as the number of every object the findings cite - Theorem 3.2.9, Remark 2.4.4, Proposition 5.6.2, Theorem 6.6.1, Lemma B.1.1, Definition 4.3.4, Proposition 5.2.4, Proposition 6.3.3, Theorem 4.5.3, Lemma 3.1.1, Example 3.2.10. I also confirmed that the published page numbers in the locators are the journal's own (the proof of Theorem 4.5.3 is on p. 41 and the section 5.6 passage on p. 51, as recorded).

Coverage was 109 of 111. The two objects with no locator were Example 4.1.1 and Remark 4.1.2, the two numbered statements that precede the extraction's first section 4.1 item (Definition 4.1.3). Both carry content the later sections use: 4.1.1 is the classifying-stack example [S/G] with the identification of 2-morphisms that Definitions 4.3.3-4.3.4 rely on, and 4.1.2 is the compatibility of the (f^*, Rf_*) adjunction with 2-morphisms, whose two commuting diagrams are used whenever section 4.3 pushes a 2-morphism through a unit or counit. I have added them as items 127 and 128, routed to the v-stack Part II beside their neighbours. That is the only change to the extraction besides the review blocks.

Internal references. I audited all 161 references of the form '<word> \ref{label}' against the environment carrying the label, resolving the seven labels my first pass could not: there is no mismatch, no duplicate label and no undefined reference.

Statuses. There are no library items, which is right: nothing in this paper's subject is in the pinned libraries. The 22 planned items and the routes cite 25 layers between them; all 25 exist in data/atlas.json.

Routes. Three Part IIs and two source routes, all accepted; see the route verdicts. All three Part II titles reproduce their parents' verbatim. Unlike most extractions I have reviewed today, these three Part IIs are proposed by this extraction alone, so the duplication check had to be done against the atlas rather than against sibling proposals: the parents demonstrably stop short (HS0-HS4, VS0-VS5, SR.0-SR.6), 'Kottwitz conjecture' appears nowhere in data/atlas.json, the only 'Lefschetz' roadmap is LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles (a different subject), and the one atlas layer that mentions cohomological correspondences is the scheme-level interface this extraction uses as a source route.

Mistakes in the paper. All 14 are confirmed, each verbatim in the hash-verified source and, where I checked, in the published text at the recorded page. Most are settled by the paper against itself: Groth(G_b(F)) described as representations of G(F) next to Groth(G(F) x W_E) (E1); (3.3.3) saying 'rho_G is the sum of the positive roots' where pp. 12 and 15 both say 2rho_G (E5); the section 3.4 announcement of the transfer operator with G(F)-coinvariants as target where Definition 6.3.2 has G_b(F) (E6); a closure written as a union of S_nu instead of S_{nu'}, and a chi_c(U, S_V) with no U defined beside a display that uses chi_c(X_nu, S_V) (E9); the middle line of a three-line display carrying rank V_mu[lambda'] where the lines above and below carry rank V_mu[lambda] (E10); Lambda-modules indexed by an undefined m where the induction runs on k (E12); G(Q_p) and G_b(Q_p) for a group over a finite extension F (E13); and a tensor product whose target should be A_1' boxtimes A_2' (E14). The one entry classified as an error, E3, is the claim that H^1(F, N(T,G)) classifies conjugacy classes of rational maximal tori; the correct statement is the kernel of H^1(F, N(T,G)) -> H^1(F,G), and the entry is right that the proof uses only well-definedness and finiteness.

Verdict: accept.
